name: Almondbanketletter
instructions: Firstly, the marzipan filling needs to be made (see marzipan recipe)
The marzipan should be rolled into a log shape about 3cm diameter and wrapped in wax paper and let rest in refrigerator overnight.
In the same day, in a large bowl, combine flour, salt, and coarsely cut butter
Add water slowly, drop by drop, and mix with wooden spoon until you have a dough mass
Have cold hands when you roll the dough into a dough ball
Using a lighter hand, pickup the dough ball and roll it into a square
Keep turning the square dough, brushing both sides with residual flour
Push superfluous flour to the side and try not to incorporate it into the dough

Fold dough into 3 pieces lengthwise, then fold it again into 3 pieces across the width. Roll it out into a square and fold it into 3 x 3 again (do this twice). After the rolling and folding 3 times, let the folded dough rest in fridge for 45-60 minutes
Repeat the roll and fold and rest process 2 more times. Make sure that the dough is thinner each time you roll it out.
After the final roll and fold, let the dough rest for 4 hours or overnight in the fridge
The next day (or after the long rest), preheat oven to 350˚F
Roll out the dough that has been folded many times into a thin sheet (0.1cm thin). We typically do 20-24 inch by as long as necessary to make the dough thin enough

Place the marzipan log on the dough about 3 cm away from an edge and roll the dough around the log. Cut the dough when the log is fully wrapped (leaving a little bit for sealing). Seal the edge with a little water
Repeat until all logs are wrapped.
Optionally form a letter or a candy cane shape with the wrapped logs. Oma always did candy cane shapes so that more fit on the baking sheet
Make sure that the dough seams are on the bottom when placing on the baking sheet and that the ends are closed and tucked under
Bake for 45 minutes at 350˚F until golden brown
To serve, cut the Almondbanketletter into 3 cm slices and serve

additional_context.story: Oma would make Almondbanketletter for all of her 21 grandchildren every Christmas so she formed them into candy canes and crammed the baking sheets.
additional_context.tips: Oma made the marzipan about 3 months ahead of christmas because it made it better (we never asked why but she was adamant that it was better this way). And she always made the dough the day before she baked it. Do not rush the rest between roll and folds as the butter needs to be cold for the flakes to be distinct. Oma was all about efficiency and so she would always make the shape as a candy cane so that she could fit more on a single baking sheet, but if you have time, the letters are fun
